q-20138.name: Question 1
q-20138.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(1,2,-1)$, $B(2,3,1)$, $C(4,1,2)$, and $D(1,4,2).$
q-20138.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i+3j+k)-(i+2j-k) \\  & =i+j+2k \\  & =⟨1,1,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(4i+j+2k)-(i+2j-k) \\  & =3i-j+3k \\  & =⟨3,-1,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(i+4j+2k)-(i+2j-k) \\  & =2j+3k \\  & =⟨0,2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =((-1)\cdot 3-2\cdot 3)-(3\cdot 3-0\cdot 3)+2(3\cdot 2-0\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-9-9+12 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-6|=6.
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

q-73733.name: Question 2
q-73733.problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨-1,1,1⟩$, $b=⟨2,1,0⟩$, and $c=⟨k,-2,-3⟩$ are coplanar.
q-73733.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ k & -2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ k & -3\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ k & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(1\cdot (-3)-(-2)\cdot 0)-(2\cdot (-3)-k\cdot 0)+(2\cdot (-2)-k\cdot 1) \\  & =3+6-4-k \\  & =5-k.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 5-k & =0 \\ k & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=5.$

q-128475.name: Question 3
q-128475.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD},$ given the points $A(7,6,4),$ $B(8,5,9),$ $C(7,4,2),$ and $D(5,7,4).$
q-128475.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(8i+5j+9k)-(7i+6j+4k) \\  & =i-j+5k \\  & =⟨1,-1,5⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(7i+4j+2k)-(7i+6j+4k) \\  & =-2j-2k \\  & =⟨0,-2,-2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(5i+7j+4k)-(7i+6j+4k) \\  & =-2i+j \\  & =⟨-2,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =((-2)\cdot 0-1\cdot (-2))+(0\cdot 0-(-2)\cdot (-2))+5(0\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot (-2)) \\  & =2-4-20 \\  & =-22.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-22|=22.
$$

q-280770.problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $x=⟨1,k,2⟩$, $y=⟨5,-2,3⟩$, and $z=⟨-4,k,1⟩$ are coplanar.

Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & k & 2 \\ 5 & -2 & 3 \\ -4 & k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}|-k\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -4 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-2\cdot 1-3\cdot k)-k(5\cdot 1-3\cdot -4)+2(5k-(-2)(-4)) \\  & =-2-3k-k(5+12)+2(5k-8) \\  & =-2-3k-17k+10k-16 \\  & =-10k-18\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =0 \\ -10k-18 & =0 \\ k & =-\frac{9}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-\frac{9}{5}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i-3j+4k)-(-i+1k) \\  & =3i-3j+3k \\  & =⟨3,-3,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-2i-2j+2k)-(-i+1k) \\  & =-i-2j+1k \\  & =⟨-1,-2,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(-j+5k)-(-i+1k) \\  & =i-j+4k \\  & =⟨1,-1,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 3 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}|-(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(-8+1)+3(-4-1)+3(1-(-2)) \\  & =-21-15+9 \\  & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-27|=27.
